quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Look left and right to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that appear to be stopped.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left and right to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: At places where people may cross your path or traffic lines meet, look left and right to make sure no one is coming.

questions.question: A large truck ahead is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. The truck:

options.text: May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
May need to swing wide to complete the right turn.
Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need extra space and must swing wide to complete a right turn.

questions.question: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: For drivers 21 or older, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is illegal. Driving under the influence is dangerous and against the law.

questions.question: At intersections with a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Give the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
Give the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.
Always slow down and go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Give the right-of-way to any traffic that is close enough to create a conflict.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Nighttime driving is more dangerous because you cannot see as well. Stay farther behind the car in front in case it stops suddenly. Use your headlights correctly and avoid looking directly at oncoming headlights.

questions.question: If a tire blows out, you should:

options.text: Press the brake hard and hold it.
Grip the steering wheel tightly and brake gently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the steering wheel tightly and brake gently.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel tightly and keep the vehicle straight. Slow down gradually by taking your foot off the gas and braking lightly. Pull off the road safely when possible.

questions.question: You enter a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. You should:

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you reach the intersection.
Turn your front wheels left to prepare to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: When turning left, signal about 100 feet before the turn. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This prevents another vehicle from pushing you into oncoming traffic if it hits you from behind.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it is dark and hard to see, stay farther behind other vehicles. Use your headlights correctly. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights as the glare can blind you.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slow down and do not use your brakes.
Slow down; the road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down; the road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Slowly reduce your speed to let them pass you.
Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Tap your brakes to slow down, then speed up again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly reduce your speed to let them pass you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, change lanes if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slowly reduce your speed. This encourages the tailgater to pass you.

questions.question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, what can they do?

options.text: They may use the left lane.
They may cut through all lanes.
They may wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists ride with traffic on the road. It is normal to see a bicyclist in the left lane when turning left.

questions.question: If your car begins to skid out of control, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, do not use the brakes. Keep steering until the vehicle is under control and moving safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to dangerous conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what must you do?

options.text: Must yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause conflict.
Must yield to vehicles only on your right.
Should slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause conflict.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, give the right-of-way to traffic already in the lanes you want to enter or cross. Be ready to stop, but you can continue if there is no traffic in your way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane is ending ahead. Drivers in that lane must merge into another lane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and use a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: If heavy smoke covers the road ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers and continue.
Reduce your speed, move as far to the right as possible, and stop off the roadway.
Turn on your high beam headlights and continue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed, move as far to the right as possible, and stop off the roadway.
questions.explanation: If heavy smoke covers the road ahead, slow down immediately, drive as far right as you can, and stop off the road. Then decide if it is safe to continue. Some smoke can harm your eyes, lungs, or health.

questions.question: You approach an intersection with a steady yellow light and have not entered yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a safe stop.
questions.explanation: At a steady yellow light, stop safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through at a safe speed.

questions.question: What color are regulatory signs?
questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers the laws they must follow. These laws cover traffic direction, lane use, turns, speed, parking, and special situations. Regulatory signs are usually white squares or rectangles with black, red, or green letters or symbols.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, after setting the parking brake, what should you do with the front wheels?

options.text: Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb. When parking uphill without a curb or when parking downhill, turn the wheels toward the curb or road edge.

questions.question: You must give the right-of-way to pedestrians who are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing the street, whether in a marked or unmarked crosswalk. For safety, always give pedestrians the right-of-way when they are crossing any street.

questions.question: Roads are slippery when it first starts to rain. On a slippery road, you should:

options.text: Avoid making turns and stops while driving at high speeds.
Test your tires' traction while going uphill.
Decrease the distance you look ahead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making turns and stops while driving at high speeds.
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tire traction. Drive slower on wet roads than on dry roads. Avoid fast turns or stops to prevent skidding.

questions.question: This sign is a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to dangers ahead, such as a change in traffic direction, a steep downgrade, or other hazards that need your attention.

questions.question: Your license can be suspended if you are under 21 and drive with a blood alcohol level of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: There is zero tolerance for alcohol if you are under 21. Any trace of alcohol in your system can result in serious penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: You want to park uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels away from the road center. This way, if your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: Broken yellow lines on streets and highways are used to:

options.text: Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Broken lines mean passing is allowed when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You may pass on the right shoulder of the road:

options.text: When the car in front of you is driving too slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder. Never leave the pavement to pass another car.

questions.question: When should drivers use high beam headlights?
questions.correctAnswerText: On open country roads
questions.explanation: Use high beams only on open country roads when no other cars are nearby. Drive slower at night than during the day.

questions.question: You are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing lights or a siren, finish crossing the intersection safely. Then drive to the right and stop. Always yield to emergency vehicles.

questions.question: A broken yellow centerline means:

options.text: Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline allows you to pass on the left when no oncoming traffic is coming. Never cross a solid yellow centerline to pass.
